Build a Shipment module · 2 of 4
Event handlers · the shipping logic

Three handlers carry the shipping flow.
All three subscribe to Payment Base events.

1. Reserve stock on contract creation
class StockReservationHandler implements HandlerInterface
{
    public static function getHandledEventClass(): string
    {
        return ContractCreatedEvent::class;
    }

    public function handle(object $event): void
    {
        $contract = $event->getContext()->getContract();
        foreach ($contract->getBasket()->getItems() as $item) {
            $this->inventory->reserve(
                articleId: $item->getArticleId(),
                quantity: $item->getQuantity(),
                contractId: $contract->getId()
            );
        }
    }
}
2. Create shipment on payment capture
class ShippingFulfillmentHandler implements HandlerInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly CarrierAdapterRegistry $carriers,
        private readonly ShipmentRepository $shipments,
        private readonly LoggerInterface $logger,
    ) {}

    public static function getHandledEventClass(): string
    {
        return PaymentCapturedEvent::class;
    }

    public function handle(object $event): void
    {
        $orderId = $event->getContext()->getOrderId();
        $carrier = $this->carriers->get($this->pickCarrierFor($orderId));

        try {
            $shipment = $carrier->createShipment(
                $this->buildRequestFor($orderId)
            );
            $this->shipments->save($shipment);
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            $this->logger->error(
                'Shipment creation failed',
                ['orderId' => $orderId, 'err' => $e->getMessage()]
            );
            // Don't rethrow — other handlers continue.
        }
    }
}
3. Release stock on cancel / expire
class StockRestorationHandler implements HandlerInterface
{
    public static function getHandledEventClass(): string
    {
        // Multi-event handlers register one class per event,
        // or use a registered alias under the same priority.
        return ContractCancelledEvent::class;
    }

    public function handle(object $event): void
    {
        $contractId = $event->getContext()->getContract()->getId();
        $this->inventory->releaseReservation($contractId);
    }
}

// services.yaml · same handler, two events
StockRestorationHandler:
    tags:
      - { name: payment.event_handler, priority: 0 }
StockRestorationHandlerOnExpiry:
    class: StockRestorationHandler
    tags:
      - { name: payment.event_handler, priority: 0 }
    # event class chosen via factory + handles ContractExpiredEvent
Best practices baked in
  • Idempotency. Webhooks may fire twice. Check oe_payments_idempotency via IdempotencyRepositoryInterface before acting.
  • Don’t rethrow. One slow carrier call must not block the rest of the chain.
  • Queue slow work. Hand label creation to a queue; event handlers stay fast.
  • Test the handler in isolation. Mock interfaces, not classes.
Notice what’s absent: no StripeClient. No PayPalApi. The shipping module is genuinely PSP-agnostic. If we add Klarna tomorrow, the shipping module learns nothing about it — the event arrives identically because Payment Base owns the event shape.
